Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/four_cut_and_heawood_reproduction.py 5; directly reconstructed dual faces for n=3..8 and reproduced the rectangular core's critical sets and complete directed Hasse acyclicity; at n=4 the core gives six critical 3-cells and the dual has 24 additional transversal triangles.
correctness.rationale: The frozen theorem is true, but the frozen uniform critical-cell calculation (RESULT.md lines 35–46) is not established by its column-extension paragraph: it asserts the surviving configurations and persistence of old terminal statuses without tracking which deletion/insertion pairs are still available when new-column pivots are interleaved with old ones. The finite tests do not fill this gap and no false critical count at any n was found. The replacement proof in repairs/5/RESULT.md proves the same claim without that matching. Edge-component counting in the bipartite row–column incidence graph proves exactly the row/rectangle core and the 6*C(n,3) additional maximal triangles. The closure F -> rows(F)×columns(F) retracts the face poset up to homotopy onto the face poset of a product-of-simplices subcomplex. Keeping a spanning tree of row edges first gives a subcomplex homotopy equivalent to two suspensions of the column simplex's 2-skeleton, each a wedge of C(n-1,3) three-spheres. The third row edge times the column triangles contributes C(n,3) more 3-cells with null attaching maps into this 2-connected subcomplex. Each additional transversal triangle then attaches by a null loop, producing the stated S² summands. Integral Alexander duality on precisely 3n vertices gives degrees 3n-6 and 3n-5 and the nonshellability obstruction. The replacement also gives the explicit disconnected quadruple establishing nonvacuous purity for n>=4.
residual_risks: Finite replication does not establish uniform critical-set claims; the repaired argument does not rely on them. No homotopy equivalence for the original complex or equivariant result is asserted.
